samples.summary: The new 742-line jsx-nodes suite is not run by any CI lane — nothing enforces it
samples.evidence: `packages/design-editor/package.json` adds `"test": "vitest --run"`, but `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only invokes vitest for `@wafflebase/sheets` (line 57), `@wafflebase/cli` (60), `@wafflebase/docs` (63) and jest for backend (66); grep for `design-editor` in ci.yml returns no matches. The reviewed change also adds no workflow step. The suite's own header claims it is "the only thing standing between a numbering change and a corrupted source file" — but a test nobody runs provides zero regression protection; a future edit to child numbering would land green.

samples.summary: Test comment claims an assertion it does not make ('an equality between the two sources, not just `located`')
samples.evidence: In `it('allows structural edits on a child of a directly-reached fragment')` the comment says "the assertion is an equality between the two sources, not just `located`", yet the body only asserts `expect(without.located).toBe(true)` and `expect(withFragment.located).toBe(true)` (lines 231-232). No equality between the two results is asserted, so the stated invariant "wrapping in a fragment must not change what is editable" is only weakly covered (e.g. differing `reason`/`relocated` would not be caught). The comment overstates the coverage the test provides.

samples.summary: `pushFnBody`'s block-body branch (returns inside a `.map(d => { ... return <li/> })`) has no test
samples.evidence: `pushFnBody` has two distinct paths: expression body (line 381) and block body walked for `return` statements while skipping nested functions (lines 384-390). Every callback fixture in the test file uses a concise expression body (`items.map(d => <li/>)` at test lines 154, 168, 178, 253, 543; `useMemo(() => <Memo/>, [])` at 159). The only block-bodied callback tested is `useEffect(() => { return () => cleanup(); }, [])` (line 631), which asserts the component root, not that a block callback's returned JSX is numbered/scoped. So `{items.map(d => { if (x) return <li/>; return <p/>; })}` numbering and iteration scoping are untested.
searchedFor: read whole test file for '=> {' callback fixtures

samples.summary: nodeAt/walkJsx agreement cross-check uses a fixture with no expressions, fragments, ternaries or iteration
samples.evidence:
The 'agrees with walkJsx about every path that exists' test (line 518) runs against `function C(){ return
; }` — plain nested elements only. The paths where the two implementations could realistically diverge (expression children `{cond && }`, ternary branches, transparent fragments, `.map` bodies) are never cross-checked; only one narrow scope case exists (line 542). A divergence in expression handling between `childrenOf` used by `walkJsx` and `nodeAt` would not fail this test.

samples.summary: No test for the dominant real-world root shape `export const Foo = () => <div/>` / `export default function` anonymous
samples.evidence: `findJsxRoots` registers arrow/function-expression consts via `ts.isVariableStatement` (line 491) and default exports via modifier check (line 470). The tests only use non-exported `const B = () => <div/>;` (test line 555) and a named `export default function Page()` (562). The exported-const form (`export const Page = () => …`), which is the common React idiom and goes through the same VariableStatement branch but wrapped in export modifiers, is never asserted; nor is the anonymous `export default () => <div/>` case (where the code leaves `defaultExport` null, undocumented by any test).
searchedFor: grep 'export const' and 'export default' in test file

samples.summary: `isReturnsRoot` is only asserted true; no negative case
samples.evidence: Line 89 asserts `isReturnsRoot(root.node)` is true. Nothing asserts it is false for `null`, `undefined`, a plain object, or a real `ts.Node` — so an implementation that returned `true` unconditionally would still pass every test in the file that uses it.

samples.summary: The `callback`-scope structural refusal (and its 'a/an' article branch) is untested
samples.evidence: Only the `iteration` refusal is asserted (test line 252-257, `expect(r.scope).toBe('iteration')`). The `callback` scope is exercised for numbering (test line 158) but never passed through `resolveNode` with `requireStatic: true`, so the second half of the ternary at jsx-nodes.mjs:731 and the callback refusal path have no coverage.
searchedFor: read resolveNode describe and owner describe blocks

samples.summary: `tagOf`'s fragment branch ('<>') and the exported `childrenOf` / `IDENTITY_ATTRS` are never exercised directly
samples.evidence: `tagOf` returns '<>' for a fragment (line 119), but fragments are transparent so `walkJsx` never yields one; no test calls `tagOf` on a fragment node, so that branch is uncovered. `childrenOf` and `IDENTITY_ATTRS` are public exports but are not imported by the test file (imports at test lines 2-15) — they are only covered incidentally through `walkJsx`/`fpOf`.

finding.summary: The new 742-line jsx-nodes suite is not run by any CI lane — nothing enforces it
finding.evidence: `packages/design-editor/package.json` adds `"test": "vitest --run"`, but `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only invokes vitest for `@wafflebase/sheets` (line 57), `@wafflebase/cli` (60), `@wafflebase/docs` (63) and jest for backend (66); grep for `design-editor` in ci.yml returns no matches. The reviewed change also adds no workflow step. The suite's own header claims it is "the only thing standing between a numbering change and a corrupted source file" — but a test nobody runs provides zero regression protection; a future edit to child numbering would land green.

verdict.reason: The jsx-nodes suite IS run and gated by CI, via an indirection the reviewer did not follow. ci.yml's verify-self job runs `pnpm verify:self` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:53-54), which is `node ./scripts/verify-self.mjs` (package.json:20). That runner's lane list includes `{ name: "verify:fast", cmd: "pnpm verify:fast" }` (scripts/verify-self.mjs:73), and any non-zero lane exit sets `failed` and exits 1 (scripts/verify-self.mjs:329-340, 358-360), so the lane is blocking. `verify:fast` ends with `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/design-editor typecheck && pnpm --filter @wafflebase/design-editor test` (package.json:12), which resolves to `vitest --run` (packages/design-editor/package.json:9). design-editor is inside the pnpm workspace (pnpm-workspace.yaml:1-2), it has no vitest config file, so vitest's default include `**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)` matches packages/design-editor/test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs, which is a genuine vitest suite (line 1 imports describe/expect/it from vitest). The reviewer's literal grep result is accurate, but this repo deliberately does not enumerate packages in ci.yml — it delegates package enumeration to the verify:self/verify:fast harness. A numbering regression would fail verify:fast, hence the verify-self job, hence CI.
